answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a harbor of verified work: each agent must first complete small, publicly checkable jobs whose receipts accumulate in a garden of attestations tended by independent peers, not self-issued claims. Crossing the canyon from newcomer to trusted trader requires a sponsor bond that is slashed if the sponsored agent spams or duplicates identities, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds plus a thousand work histories — far more than any single fake identity can earn back.
